title: Q3 Enterprise Private Deploy: Prioritization, Acceptance Criteria, and Release Gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define and socialize the Q3 roadmap slice for enterprise Private/VPC/on-prem deployments focused on (1) a prioritized set of features and compat gates customers need for production adoption, (2) explicit acceptance criteria per feature and per infra-mode, and (3) release gates & pilot plan to minimize upgrade incidents. Scope: acceptance matrix for RBAC/KMS/upgrade flows, SLA and latency SLO mapping for private vs dedicated, upgrade rollback/runbook verification, pilot cohort selection, and telemetry + evals to measure regressions. Success metrics: pilot customers onboarded (>=3), pass rate of acceptance tests >=95% across pilot infra, no SEV incidents related to upgrade in first 30 days post-release, and documented roll-forward plan and automation for compatibility checks.
updates: 2026-01-20: Kickoff meeting with Eng (runtime), Security, and Solutions — aligned on top enterprise asks: KMS integration permutations, RBAC parity, and upgrade windows.
2026-02-03: Draft acceptance criteria matrix shared; requested additional rows for quantization/compatibility with older GPU drivers.
2026-02-18: UX/Console team flagged dashboard telemetry gaps for per-route latency SLOs in private environments.
2026-02-25: Narrowed pilot cohort to three customers (healthcare, fintech, adtech) and agreed on non-production staging windows for each.
2026-03-01: Dependency list finalized — ENG to deliver automated preflight checks; Security to complete KMS threat model.
2026-03-08: PM review with GTM — packaging and pricing notes captured for pilot contractual terms.
2026-03-10: Acceptance matrix v0.3 posted and reviewers requested; next: engineering estimates for gating automation.
review_feedback: Design (Sofia Tran): request clearer console flows for 'compatibility failures' with suggested inline remediation links.
Eng Lead (Ravi Kapoor): prefer feature toggles and canary rollout per-customer; recommended reducing initial scope to core KMS and RBAC parity only.
Security (Lina Gomez): require explicit KMS rotation acceptance criteria and audit log retention minimums before pilot approval.
GTM (Nora Chen): pilot contract needs explicit SLA credits and runbook access obligations for customers.
decisions: Scope trimmed for Q3 pilot: core KMS integrations (AWS KMS + GCP KMS), RBAC feature parity, and automated preflight upgrade checks.
Rollout strategy: per-customer canary with automatic rollback on integrity or SLO regressions; no platform-wide flip for Q3.
Acceptance metric threshold: >=95% success on automated acceptance tests across all pilot environments for release to wider GA.
Trade-off: postpone full driver/quantization compatibility matrix to Q4 to reduce scope and unblock pilot cadence.
next_steps: Eng: provide story-level estimates for automating preflight checks by 2026-03-20 (owner: Ravi).
Security: complete KMS threat model and sign off acceptance rows by 2026-03-18 (owner: Lina).
Design: add inline remediation links and small console CTAs for compat failures (deliverable 2026-03-22, owner: Sofia).
PM: finalize pilot SOW and GTM playbook draft for review with Legal & Sales by 2026-03-24 (owner: Marco).
Schedule pilot onboarding windows with the three customers and confirm staging resources by 2026-03-28.
